```suggestion
			remove_android_build_template->popup_centered_clamped(Size2(600, 200) * EDSCALE, 0.7);
```

To prevent cutoff  in Android Editor, due to wide REMOVE_ANDROID_BUILD_TEMPLATE_MESSAGE.

This logic only checks for the `default template` and `gradle_build/android_source_template`. It does not check when the template was installed from a file.

As a result, even when the template has been installed from a file, the Project Export window still incorrectly reports that the template is not installed and asks to install the default template.

If a valid template is already installed then, the `Install Android Build Template` project menu options does nothing.

If this method is called for this menu, and if template is already installed then it should shows the `remove_android_build_template` dialog like it previously did.

```suggestion
					err += vformat(TTR("Invalid build directory (version mismatch). Manually delete \"%s\" or enable automatic deletion in the Editor Settings (Export > Android > Build > Automatically Delete Build Directory)."), ExportTemplateManager::get_android_build_directory(p_preset)) + "\n";
```
Always better to provide more context.

`Version mismatch` is but one cause for an invalid build directory. There could be other issues including accidental deletion of the `.build_version` metadata file, or directory access issue. 
So because of that, the error message is necessarily vague.
